prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

Title, set largest at the top left of the page: extract-text
Deck beneath it: The words are lifted clean off a scanned page — headers, page numbers, and broken hyphens left behind — and laid down as marked pages of markdown.

Hero: a large scanned book page stands at the left, drawn as a worn sheet with its parts labeled where they sit: a shouted running header across its top, a bare page number in its corner, body paragraphs in the middle, and at the bottom edge a word split by a hyphen. From this sheet, the body text alone lifts away as a translucent layer, drawn peeling up and toward the right, leaving header, number, and footer greyed on the old sheet beneath. A note at the peel: only the body comes along; the furniture of the page stays behind.

The lifted layer settles at the right onto a clean fresh sheet, where the same paragraphs sit renewed, headed by a small typeset comment reading <!-- page 41 -->. A note beside it: every page carries its marker — the thread the later stages navigate by.

Between the two sheets, three small joinery details drawn as watchmaker's insets in a vertical run:
- a split word, dis- above and covery below, drawn being spliced into one whole word with a fine joint;
- the tail of a sentence at one page's foot curving across a gap to meet its continuation at the next page's head, captioned: a paragraph broken by the page break is stitched back together;
- a short line of small capitals rising to become a headline with a flourish, captioned: a lone capitals line opening a page becomes the chapter's heading.

One quiet inset at the lower left: a fork in a path — one branch dives into the book itself, the other runs to a small archive building on the horizon — captioned: good embedded text is taken straight from the scan; a poor scan borrows the archive's typed copy instead.

One warm accent colour follows the lifted text layer and the spliced joins; both sheets and the furniture stay in ink.
